articleTitle: Modern load profile for standalone PV rural household in Malaysia
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This study presents a modern load profile (Load Profile 2.0) for a 660 square feet rural household where modern lifestyle of the occupants and home appliances are considered. This load profile is compared against a dated load profile of a standalone PV rural household with battery system (Load Profile 1.0) which is recorded in 2008. Both load profiles are tested in a similar standalone PV system with battery system, which is constructed in 2008, to present the adaptability of the dated standalone PV system to updated Load Profile 2.0. The detailed experimental result of both load profiles are presented. The results highlight that the standalone PV system with battery is able to supply energy to Load Profile 2.0 without failure while maintaining the battery SOC above 62%.

articleTitle: Reduction of switching transients in CC/CV mode of electric vehicles battery charging
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Constant current (CC) / Constant voltage (CV) is the most optimum algorithm applied for lithium-ion battery charging used in EVs. However, major issue during this mode of charging are the switching transients. Subsequently, smooth transition from CC to CV is required for minimizing switching losses and increasing the battery life expectancy. Generally, toggle switch is used to transit from CC to CV. It operates (CC to CV), when the output voltage reaches to predefined value of voltage. But due to the ripple in the output voltage, toggle switch changes its state from ON to OFF and OFF to ON. Hence, the output of the controller oscillate between CC to CV continuously. To mitigate this problem, a novel charging method, using Schmitt trigger, for optimum transition from CC to CV is proposed in this paper. Schmitt trigger operates in a specified band limit, which is decided by the voltage ripple. To verify this scheme, boost converter is modeled and its controllers for CC and CV mode are designed. Proposed scheme is implemented in MATLAB using real time simulator Opal-RT.

articleTitle: Classification of the harmonic load types using multi-layer extreme learning machine
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This paper presents a neural network approach intended to aid electricity consumers or power system planner in the task of classification of harmonic load types using the measurements (data samples) collected from one of the power station in Malaysia. In order to allow the classification of the type of harmonic loads, harmonic currents order produced by aggregate harmonic loads and the level of emission are modelled using the Multi-Layer Extreme Learning Machine with autoencoder (hereinafter denoted as ML-ELM-AE). The feasibility of ML-ELM-AE on the classification of the Harmonic empirical data set will be probed, for when the classification results of the Harmonic load types become available, it can come in handy to power system analyst or engineers for analysis in later stage. They can use it to determine the harmonic distortion patterns and to characterize the harmonic currents at network buses. Depending on whether the aggregate load is residential, commercial, or industrial, the load characteristics in terms of its harmonic contents are likely to be different. The achieved results demonstrate the effectiveness of the investigated technique in dealing with the real world power system application of harmonic load type classification, that can be useful in providing good indication to the power system or distribution network planner.

articleTitle: Impacts of large-scale solar photovoltaic generation on power system frequency response
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: The increasing share of renewable energy integrated into the electricity networks, particular solar photovoltaic systems has introduced new operational challenges to grid operators. As the solar output is highly intermittent, the occurrence of power mismatch in the system will increase. Furthermore, the converter-based solar photovoltaic (PV) plant has zero inertia which will inevitably reduce the overall system's inertia and cause stability problem in the event of contingency or large power mismatch. In this regard, this paper aims to investigate the impacts of large-scale solar PV plant on power system's frequency response. Two IEEE test systems have been considered in this study, namely the IEEE 9 bus, and IEEE 39 bus test systems to investigate how different levels of large scale solar PV penetrations will impact on the overall system frequency response. The results suggest that the increasing share of solar generation in the generation mix will result in the reduction of total system inertia. Hence, the system becomes more susceptible to disturbance and contingency events. The study also shows that the system will collapse during the worst case contingency situation when the solar PV penetrations are over 40% of the system's generating capacity.

articleTitle: Buck-boost converter with q-ZSC topology
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: An impedance source buck-boost converter is proposed. Utilizing the q-ZSC topology, the converter has a gain curve of the buck-boost converter. This gain curve gives it advantage over a corresponding regular q-ZSC because under a given duty ratio, it has a gain greater by magnitude 1. When operated at a duty ratio of 0.677, it has a gain of −2.1 compared to −1.1 for the regular q-ZSC, signifying an increased gain of 90.9%. The equation relating the gains of the two converters was also derived. Its additional capacitor and inductor belong to its impedance network thus permitting higher frequency operation, elimination of dead time, shoot-through effects etc. gives it advantage over a corresponding traditional buck-boost converter. Its operation and a corresponding buck-boost converter are compared and analyzed.

articleTitle: Design of double stator slotted rotor for large ceiling fan application
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: The large ceiling fan is often attribute to the weather which is environmentally warm and humid conditions. Usually, IM has low starting torque compared to other DC motor. But IM need to be attached with the gear mounted on the ceiling to reduce the speed. This contributes to the main problem of this application which is noise and vibration due to gear. In this research, the aim is to design a BLDC motor with of Double Stator Slotted Rotor Brushless DC Motor (DSSR-BLDC) topology to overcome the problem occurs in large ceiling fan application. Initially, DSSR-BLDC is designed using Permeance Analysis Method (PAM) to determine the motor sizing. By using PAM, the magnetic flux is calculated using magnetic circuit and mathematical modelling based on the direction of flux which flows in stator, rotor and air gaps. Secondly, the DSSR-BLDC model is analyze using Finite Element Method (FEM) to predict the back emf (BEMF), static torque and the transient torque. The result shows the DSSR-BLDC is able to produce 45 Nm of torques and fulfill the design restrictions. Finally, this research provides an overview of designing DSSR-BLDC for large ceiling fan application.

articleTitle: Optimal placement and sizing of distributed generation based on MVMO-SH
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid variant mean-variance mapping optimization (MVMO-SH) algorithm to optimize distributed generation (DG) sites and sizes in the grid network. The objective function is to minimize power loss. The proposed MVMO-SH algorithm is applied on standard IEEE-30 bus test system to examine the usefulness and effectiveness of the method in solving problems related to sitting and sizing of distributed generation in transmission system. A reduction in transmission system's total power loss and improvement in voltage profiles have been shown with appropriate sizes and sites of DG in power system network.

articleTitle: Optimization of neural network hyperparameters for gas turbine modelling using Bayesian optimization
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Gas turbine model can be used for many applications that can improve gas turbine operation's efficiency and reliability. Artificial Neural Network (ANN) was identified as a good technique for gas turbine modelling. However, ANN is sensitive to its hyperparameters. Current approaches for optimizing the hyperparameters of ANN used in gas turbine modelling has high computational cost. Hence, this paper proposes optimizing the ANN hyperparameters using Bayesian optimization. Bayesian optimization was used to determine the near-optimum number of layers and number of neurons for the developed gas turbine model. The result shows hyperparameters optimization using Bayesian optimization results neural network with better prediction accuracy compared to hyperparameters optimization using random search.

articleTitle: Optimization for the planning of distributed renewable generators using genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: The integration of distributed generators (DGs) considering renewable energy provides great benefits to the distribution networks, such as, reductions in power loss and improvements of voltage profile. However, such benefits to the distribution networks are constrained with the installation of DGs with proper sizes and locations. In this paper, the optimization for sizing and placement of distributed renewable generators (DRGs) in the electrical distribution networks is presented. The optimum sizes and locations for the DRGs are determined to reduce the power loss in the distribution networks. The genetic algorithm (GA) has been used to solve the optimization problem using MATLAB. For the validation, results of this study are compared with other well-known heuristic optimization techniques and analytical approaches. The numerical studies on the IEEE 33 bus distribution network have revealed that the proposed algorithm is capable for finding the optimum size and place of DRG in the distribution networks. The optimization results using GA are seen very competitive with the result by other well-known heuristic optimization techniques and analytical approaches that have been used for the similar studies. The results from this study signify the use of GA in the research related to planning of renewable energy and power system.

articleTitle: Techno-economic analysis of lighting system retrofit at the industrial training institute
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This paper presents the lighting systems retrofit according to the European Standard EN12464-1 in an educational building of the Department of Mechanical Technology, Industrial Training Institute, Selandar, Melaka, Malaysia. The building and lighting systems simulation has carried out using DIALux software. The T5 and LED luminaires are used as alternative luminaires to replace existing T8 luminaires in the building. The analysis involved in this study are the lighting power density (LPD), lighting energy numeric indicator (LENI), energy savings potential, payback period (PP) and annualized life cycle cost (ALCC). Based on the results, by retrofitted T8 luminaires with the LED luminaires achieved energy savings of 32%, PP of 5.5 years and ALCC of RM 24,286.86. It showed that the LED luminaires provided the great performance to replace the existing luminaires due to lowest LPD, LENI, payback period and ALCC and highest energy savings compared to T8 luminaires.

articleTitle: Steady state performance analysis of one switched inductor series Z-source inverter
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Based on the classical Z-Source inverter (ZSI), this paper represents an impedance network inverter that is termed as one switched inductor (SL) series Z-source inverter because of the composing of one switched inductor cell in the circuit's series type impedance network. The traditional ZSI has high voltage stress on capacitor and low boost factor. The proposed circuit has high boost factor and low voltage stress on its impedance network capacitor. To enhance the boost ability and reduce the capacitor voltage stress simultaneously the proposed topology couples the SL cell type series impedance network to main inverter switching circuit. Two operational states of the topology have been illustrated, shoot through (ST) and non-ST mode. The simulation results done by Matlab/Simulink verifies the performance analysis of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Smart energy meter using Telegram bot
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: A smart meter in which the application designed to be able to perform two-way communication wirelessly between the meter unit with centralized units that differs from the conventional energy meter with functionality limited to measurement of total energy consumption without being able to provide any information of energy usage to the user. The issue of untracked electricity usage during the one-month period make the system vulnerable to power theft, power misused and overconsumption without prior notice to the user. The system is developed using suitable controller board and sensors to allow the system integration with conventional meter providing the smart meter functionality. The objective of the project is to design a smart meter which provide user with wireless energy monitoring functionality with the use of the Telegram bot application.

articleTitle: Islanding detection technique based on rate of change of reactive power (dq/dt)
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Islanding is a technique used to maintain the power system stable by splitting the power system into number of islands. In island mode, it becomes easy to maintain the stability of the system. In this paper, islanding detection technique based on rate of change of reactive power is presented. The strategy is implemented through simulation on PSCAD/EMTDC software. Simulation results show that the used strategies sense the islanding and differentiating islanding with other events such as addition of inductive and capacitive load.

articleTitle: Recent studies in concentrated photovoltaic system (CPV): A review
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Concentrated Photovoltaic (CPV) is an attractive alternative to fossil fuels due to its ability to reduce the PV cell area and increase the energy outputs using low cost optics. This review paper, details the recent experimental and simulation studies conducted in the field related to CPV in the past few years. The paper details the general expressions used for experimental works, followed by sections detailing the studies conducted on the optics, photovoltaics, heat dissipation and integration application. Different designs proposed by the researchers has also been briefly described. The findings shows the potential for CPV and CPV/T systems is promising with overall efficiencies greater than 60%.

articleTitle: Numerical and experimental investigation of the effect of tilt angle on the performance of PV systems
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: The photovoltaic (PV) panels and system performance is affected by the tilt angle and orientation, as these factors investigate the total amount of irradiation intensity received by the related surface of a panel. This research conducts an experiment with the variation of tilt angle under certain operating conditions. In addition, the impact of surface tilt angle with various irradiation levels on PV performance is analyzed numerically using Finite Element Method (FEM). The effect of varying the tilt angle from 0° to 80° on PV performance is studied under both variable and constant irradiation conditions. For every 100 W/m2 irradiation intensity increased, the solar cell temperature and power output increase by 5.34°C and 5.94 W for numerical as well as by 5.37°C and 5.83 W for experimental results, respectively. For every 5° increments in surface tilt angle, the average power output and solar cell temperature drop by 1.55 W and 1.12°C for numerical and by 1.59 W and 1.09°C for experimental case, while efficiency falls by 0.35% and 0.33% for experimental and numerical cases, respectively. The optimum tilt angle can maximize the irradiation on a panel and thereby the performance of the panel.

articleTitle: Experimental analysis on defect power cable with TDR technique application
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This study focuses on the experimental analysis of defect power cable with the application of time domain reflectometry (TDR) technique. TDR is a reflectometry technique where the injected signal is reflected when there is an impedance mismatch detected. A degraded cable insulation has a lower impedance compared to the ideal cable insulation. Hence, theoretically a degraded cable section can be pinpointed from the reflected signal due to the difference in impedance between these two mediums. This principle has to be investigated in actual application and thus, a series of experiments are conducted on various combinations of cable insulation condition with a single j oint using the TDR application. Results obtained from these experiments have proven that the TDR theory is practical and can be used for sectionalizing degraded cable. Section three in this paper discusses in detail the findings of all experiments conducted with the TDR application.

articleTitle: Self-tuning fuzzy logic control based on MRAS for induction motor drives
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Self-Tuning Fuzzy Logic Controller (ST-FLC) has received intensive interests in the field of Induction Motor (IM) drive system. Standard FLC always have a limit in speed operation and not robust. This paper proposes self-tuning mechanism of the fuzzy speed control using Takagi-Sugeno (TS) fuzzy type based on reference model adaption (MRAS). The proposed Self-Tuning TS based MRAS method is applied to the IM drive system in order to tune the main speed control (mamdani) online accordingly. The obtained results emphasized the ST-FLC TS enhance the performance of the drive system and force the system to follow the behaviour of the reference model. The advantage of ST can be visualized during various speed operation demand and load disturbances.

articleTitle: Impact of intermittency towards microgrid protection & reliability considering grid codes
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This paper outlined the impact of intermittent characteristics towards microgrid protection and microgrid reliability considering the latest grid codes requirement such as low voltage ride through (LVRT) and reactive current injection (RCI). These can be achieved by varying the irradiance level for microgrid protection considering different type of RCI controls. A reliability index known as Srate are introduced to represent the relationship between irradiance level and microgrid protection using overcurrent relay.

articleTitle: Ionic conductivity and molecular vibration analysis of PMMA/ENR 5O-NH4SCN polymer blend electrolytes
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Ing technique. The maximum ionic conductivity of 2.51 × 10−8 Scm−1 was achieved for sample with 12 wt.% NH4SCN at room temperature. From Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) analyses it was observed the shifting of the C=O, C-O-C and C-O stretching bands in PMMA/ENR 50-NH4SCN polymer electrolyte films. The force constant values for selected bands with various composition of salts was determined and correlated with ionic conductivity.

articleTitle: Gasification of refinery sludge using coal fly ash and refinery sludge ash as catalysts
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Gasification of dry refinery sludge has gained a lot of interest of late. Fly ash and sludge ash are waste by product of gasification process. Using these ashes as catalyst material can reduce the waste disposal to landfill sites. This study has shown that both fly ash and sludge ash can be used as a catalyst in gasification as it is rich in catalytic material like silica, alumina, ferric oxide, calcium oxide and a host of other catalytic materials. These ashes catalytic material shows improved syngas quality when blended with dry refinery sludge (DRS) in updraft gasification process thereby enhances its economic viability. Furthermore, mixing of these catalysts with sludge fuel cause reduction of the agglomeration of metal oxides inside an up draft gasifier. The presence of fly and sludge ash catalyst are found to convert stable tar into gaseous products, thus enhance the hydrogen production by moving water-gas shift reaction to forward direction. Experiments were performed to determine the catalytic effects of fly and sludge ash using various percentages ranging from 0, 10, 15 and 20% and with equivalent ratio (ER) of 0.195 and 0.24. The study was centered on the product gas, heating value, combustible gases vol%, and cold gas and carbon conversion efficiencies. It was found that both fly and sludge ash has enhanced catalytic properties. An ER of 0.195 is best suited for the gasification of dry refinery sludge. Increase in the catalyst addition improves gas quality, increases high heating value (HHV) and cold gas efficiency.

articleTitle: Solar energy transition in Malaysia through implementation of PV and PVT technologies
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Renewable energy (RE) is an important source of sustainable energy and hence has great worth to promote it. The renewable energy has been introduced since the 8th Malaysia plan as a fifth key element of the fuel policy. The goal of 5% renewable energy supply of the total energy was set. However, the achievement of the 5% renewable goal has failed. Therefore, to promote renewable energy among people of Malaysia, the aim is to propose a project to work in depth. This project is designed to investigate a case study which will perform the installation and examination of the working condition of the PV (photovoltaic) & PVT (photovoltaic thermal) in different locations of peninsular Malaysia. Opinion and experience of end users will be collected for analysis of public awareness and acceptability. The proposed work will benefit the local people of Malaysia, policymakers as well as the industry and research.

articleTitle: Mathematical modelling of PV array in MATLAB/Simulink with partial shading conditions
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Studies in maximum power point tracking of a solar PV array are conducted through modelling of a solar PV system in various scenarios using MATLAB/Simulink. However, the studies conducted lack depth in modelling of PV system if Simulink toolboxes for PV array are used and risk running slower simulations because of integration of Simscape models with the rest of the system. Furthermore, those who use mathematical modelling lack flexibility in modifying parameters to simulate conditions such as partial shading. In this paper, a Suntech STP330–24/Vfw 330W polycrystalline solar module is modelled in MATLAB/Simulink to study the effects of partial shading on a 5kWp solar system. The PV system is mathematically modelled and verified in accordance with the datasheet parameters and found to ensure accurate replication of the real system with an error of 0.0237%. A dashboard of the system is created in Simulink to quickly alter varying irradiances of individual modules and the effects of PSC on the output power of a PV array are tested. This paper provides a complete modelling approach of the PV system in MATLAB/Simulink. The model achieves high level of accuracy, flexibility in tuning parameters, real time control of temperature and insolation, and provides a platform for future research to be conducted.

articleTitle: Biodiesel impact on cost, fuel saving and emission reduction for power generation in Malaysia
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: The main objective of this paper is to assess the production cost and impact on fuel saving and emission reduction of biodiesel for power generation, using a wide range of economic indicators. Renewable fuels such as biodiesel provides many benefits especially for the developing countries. Apart from the opportunities for economic growth and development across the country, particularly for rural communities; chances are also available for independent power producers to generate power to off-grid users and local businesses. This is only achievable from engines and fuels with good economic performance. The first section looks at the biodiesel production cost within the system boundary of the feedstock farming, the crude oil extraction and the biodiesel processing. The comparison between palm biodiesel and calophyllum inophyllum (CI) biodiesel are made to highlight the benefit of using the second generation feedstock (CI biodiesel), which shows lower production cost compared to the first generation feedstock (palm biodiesel). The second section analyze the impact of CI biodiesel on the fuel saving and the CO2 emission reduction. This section focuses on the application of CI biodiesel in two different systems, namely internal combustion engines in the transport sector and gas turbines in the power sector. The results showed that application of CI biodiesel in the power sector is able to have more significant savings in fuel and reduction in the CO2 emissions.

articleTitle: Locally available material as adsorbent to treat arsenic contaminated water
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Groundwater contaminated by arsenic pose a great threat to the environment. This work investigated the efficiency of easily available and non-toxic waste such as egg shell and banana peel to treat arsenic contaminated water. Egg shell and banana peel were characterized by FTIR to see the functional group responsible for adsorption. Batch experiments were separately carried to find the removal efficiencies of two forms of arsenic: arsenite and arsenate. The effects of various parameters, like dose of adsorbent, pH, retention time, agitation speed and initial analyte concentration were investigated. The maximum arsenic adsorption was found for 2mg/L solution by egg shell with a dose of 6 g/L. 68.54 % of As(III) was adsorbed at pH 9 at an equilibrium time of 160 min while 72.01 % of As(V) was adsorbed at pH 6 at an equilibrium time of 80 min. Hence it was observed that the presence of calcium carbonate and hydroxyl group in egg shell and banana peel favoured arsenic adsorption.

articleTitle: Reduction of unbalanced armature magnetic flux in segmental rotor fefsm using rotor span refinement
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Recently, Field Excitation Flux Switching Motor (FEFSM) using salient rotor has been introduced with their advantages of overlap winding (OW) and controllable field excitation coil (FEC) magnetic flux. Despite the motor has high power and high speed diverse performances, the salient rotor structure is found to lead much longer flux path between stator and rotor producing weak flux linkage along with low torque performances. In this research, a new structure of singlephase FEFSM using segmental rotor with non-overlap windings (NOW) is proposed with clear advantages of less copper losses, light rotor weight and much robust structure. Characteristic performances of the proposed motors such as armature coil and field excitation coil flux linkages, back-emf, average torque, and output power are analysed using JMAG Designer version 15. Ratio of unbalanced armature magnetic flux has also been solved using rotor span refinement. The armature magnetic flux amplitude at positive and negative cycles have been improved by 41.5% and 69.1%, respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis and performance of 4S-8P permanent magnet flux switching motors (PMFSM) for electric bicycle applications
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Nowadays, most of the investigated electric vehicles were arranged for electric cars. Another electric vehicle that is also attractive in a broad range area are electric bicycles. In this regard, Electric bicycles are increasingly attractive as they have a high energy efficiency advantage compared to other forms of energy. Since their low investment costs, many people prefer to use an electric bicycle rather than an electric car or an electric motorcycle. One example of successfully developed in electric bicycle application is switch reluctance motor (SRM) as shown in Figure.1. However, SRM is not desirable which is noisy in vibration so make this motor unattractive in this application. The latest research of Axial Flux Permanent Magnet (AFPM) motor prepared for electric bicycle applications is shown in Figure 1. These machine can deliver high torque to weight ratio, better efficiency, lower thermal and noise problems. However, there was an inherent weakness in the design and high manufacturing cost because of the high diameter of the size design motor and permanent magnet (PM). Therefore, a new structure of 4Slot-8Pole Permanent Magnet Flux Switching Motor (PM-FSM) for the electric bicycle applications is introduced and investigated. The design, principles of operation, torque characteristics and power of this new topology are studied by JMAG-Designer through a 2D-FEA. Permanent magnet motor size and volume is designed at 85mm and 2610mm3, respectively. On the basis of the investigation, it can be concluded that the proposed PM-FSM for a single phase 4Slot 8Pole topology has achieved the small diameter design motor target with less PM weight and high torque performance, at approximately 4.9Nm with the deterministic optimization method.

articleTitle: Investigation on the load factor performance at Wisma R&D universiti Malaya building
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Load factor is one of the indicator which describe how energy is being consumed in premises. Eventhough there are various other factors such as capacity factor, use factor and others; load factor can be calculated by the customer or the premise's owner from their monthly utility bill. This study investigates the consumption characteristic of electricity in Wisma R&D, Universiti Malaya building over a period of three years through its load factor performance. By understanding the load profile of a premise, load factor improvement initiative can be put in place which will not only enhance the load balancing of the premise but will reduce its utility bill as well. The load profile presented had shown that Wisma R&D is not operating at a recommended load factor based on the threshold set by Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), which is said to be higher than 0.6. Predicted cost saving based on the TNB threshold load factor had been analyse and several immediate load factor improvement initiatives have been recommended at the end of the paper.

articleTitle: Process simulation of bio-ethanol production from empty fruit bunch via acid hydrolysis pretreatment
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This work developed bio-ethanol production process based on empty fruit bunch (EFB) of palm oil and compared it with the literature benchmark model. Dilute acid hydrolysis is used as the biomass pretreatment prior to enzyme hydrolysis and fermentation. The amount of bio-ethanol produced from the EFB is higher than that in the literature, which used corn stover as the feedstock. This is because, the content of cellulose and xylan in EFB is higher by 5.4wt% and 17wt% respectively, compared to corn stover. The estimated annual economic potentials for EFB and corn stover feed processes are $ 141 mil and $ 153 mil, respectively. The significantly lower price of EFB ($5/ton) compared to corn stover ($58.50/ton) contributes to the higher profitability of the production of bio-ethanol from EFB.

articleTitle: 4-Coils magnetic resonance coupling wireless power transfer with varying rotational angle
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This research work performs a study on Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) using 4-coils magnetic resonance where research focuses on varying the rotational angle of the receiver coil from the centre of system. Simulation work is performed using CST Microwave Studio to observe the magnetic coupling for 4-coils system at a varied rotational angle. Comparative analysis was performed at different rotational angle which are 0°, 15°, 30° and 45°. Performance parameters such as scattering parameter, impedance parameter, electric field and magnetic field are analysed.

articleTitle: Energy saving potential through energy conservation of office equipment in Malaysia polytechnic
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This paper study the energy saving potential in Malaysian Educational Institution with referring one of Malaysian Polytechnic known as Politeknik Sultan Azlan Shah (PSAS). Exercise through energy audit has been conducted in PSAS to identify energy usage of photocopiers machine. This study will analyse two types of photocopiers machine known as heavy duty machine and medium duty machine. From energy audit, the energy saving potential will estimated through the implementation of energy conservation measures. After reschedule operating hours duration of photocopier machine, it is found that energy saving potential is about 9422.8 kWh and cost saving is RM 3439.3. Overall, it is found that the energy saving potential and cost saving of 58.6% when the energy conservation proposed are implemented.

articleTitle: Harmonic minimization of a single phase cascade H-bridge multilevel inverters using firefly algorithm
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: The different topologies and control strategies of multilevel inverters (MLIs) have been studied and discussed for more than two decades due to MLIs involved in many applications. The superior performance of MLIs technology has drawn tremendous interest among researchers from industry and academia in recent years. This paper describes the use of an improved of firefly algorithms in order to find the switching angles with the optimum values of a single phase of modified cascaded H-Bridge Multilevel inverters (CHB-MLs) for five levels. Even though there are a lot of techniques of optimization in determining of switching angles, firefly algorithm still has an advantages due to this algorithm is taking less computation time and enables to minimize the harmonics problems of the output voltage and current waveforms of the modified CHB-MLIs. In order to verify the performance of the proposed algorithm an appropriate model has been developed based on MARLAB/SIMULINK. Then the simulation results demonstrate be compared with the results obtained using particle swarm optimization (PSO) and Newton Raphson (NR) algorithms and it is found that the proposed technique offers reduced total harmonic distortion (THD) of the voltage and current waveforms of modified CHB-MLIs with less computation period.

articleTitle: Public opinions towards acceptance and awareness of renewable energy technologies
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Renewable energy (RE) is an important source of sustainable energy and hence has been great worth promoting it. Since the renewable-energy technologies (RET) are increasingly using in power generation systems worldwide, public opinions on the use of new technologies are still considerable and need to be explored. For Malaysia, country's fuel policy, including renewable resources such as hydro, coal, gas, and oil, has set the target of 5% of total energy supply, but it has yet not achieved. Therefore, in order to promote renewable energy among the people of Malaysia, we aim to highlight the importance of public opinions. Here we will explain the significance of public opinions towards awareness and acceptance of renewable-energy sources and technologies. The proposed work will contribute to promoting the future use of renewable energy as clean and sustainable energy.

articleTitle: The impact of energy yield of a photovoltaic system under partial shading
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Photovoltaic module is very susceptible to partial shading problem. In a photovoltaic power system, large number of photovoltaic modules are connected in series to provide required voltage and power. Due to large number of photovoltaic modules, the chances of every photovoltaic module to receive uniform solar irradiance become lower. Therefore, a photovoltaic system consists of large number of photovoltaic modules is even more susceptible to partial shading problem. This paper presents the investigation of the energy yield of a photovoltaic system under partial shading conditions. The investigation results shows that the energy yield of a photovoltaic system decreases as the shading heaviness increases. However, the effect is not constant. The effect is especially significant when the photovoltaic system is under lightly partial shaded conditions. In worst case, the energy yield of the photovoltaic system can drops up to 17.65 % as the shading heaviness increases by 20 %. Therefore, the partial shading need to be address in order to minimize the losses of the photovoltaic system under partial shading conditions.

articleTitle: A flexible microgrid through overcurrent protection
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: As the distributed generation (DG) is being increasingly integrated into the distribution grid, the formation of the un-intentional island can happen as a natural consequence to the fault isolation processes. To ensure safety, IEEE 1547 stipulates that any unintentional island formed must be terminated as soon as possible, which is also known as the anti-islanding scheme. However, the electricity reliability can be increased by sustaining the intentional island. Recently, the concept of microgrid had been promoted for increased electricity reliability where the grid can operate in both grid-connected and islanded modes. However, the proposed microgrid has a very rigid boundary where the exact points of the split in the network had to be clearly identified. Besides that, the implementation of such microgrid would require huge capital investment in setting up the communication facilities. In contrast, this paper aims to develop a microgrid with flexible points split and using only the existing directional overcurrent relays. The proposed scheme is both flexible and economical. The fault current contributed by the static solar photovoltaic generators as compared to a synchronous generator will also be discussed in this paper. The main highlight of this paper is the challenge in grading the overcurrent relays with the much smaller fault current magnitude from the static generator.

articleTitle: Hill climbing maximum power point tracking on four stage switch capacitor based boost converter
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: In this paper, a theoretical analysis has been presented to observe the performance of the Hill Climbing (HC) Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) technique on the Four Stage Switch Capacitor Based Boost Converter (4-SCBC). To implement the HC, a 4-SCBC is connected with a resistive load. In addition, a KC85T Solar Module has been employed to witness the operational performance of the 4-SCBC to realize a Stand-Alone Photovoltaic (PV) system, while operating near MPP, at the left of MPP (LM) or at the right of MPP (RM). In order to attain software simulation results, the MATLAB Simulink was employed. Results obtained prove to be parallel in performance with the theoretical analysis presented.

articleTitle: Single-ended primary inductor converter (SEPIC) for LED application
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of a capacitor diode (CD) resistor-less snubber that is able to reduce the power loss with improved efficiency for a MOSFET switch in a single-ended primary-inductor converter (SEPIC) for LED application. There are many types of snubber circuit available in the literature; however, the basic concept literally consists of inductor, capacitor, resistor and diode. The conventional method that includes a resistor should be avoided since it promotes a higher loss in the converter. Among the most used topology for LED driver is the single-ended primary-inductor converter (SEPIC). This topology has efficiency up to 90%, small in size and weight. Another advantage using a SEPIC; it is capable of producing an output that is smaller or higher than the input, making it suitable for wide input operation. The proposed CD snubber will be tested on an isolated SEPIC with 238V input voltage, 30V output at 100kHz configuration which is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink to verify the capability of proposed snubber circuit.

articleTitle: Design of multiphase transformer using phasor method
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This paper is focusing on a development of a multiphase transformer. The development of this transformer is based on the manipulation of the phasor diagram. The two input voltage phasors are added together in order to generate the output voltage on the secondary side of the multi-phase transformer. The connection is modelled and validated in Matlab/Simulink software prior to the fabrication process. Finally, it is expected that the development of multiphase transformer can be used in for drives application and may also be further explored to be utilized in power transmission system.

articleTitle: A review of global current techniques and evaluation methods of photocatalytic CO2 reduction
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Nowadays, energy issues that derive from mass energy consumption and the climate change by the increasing concentration of carbon dioxide (CO2) in the atmosphere is a critical problem that people around the world are facing. To tackle these problems, the uses of renewable energy that mainly generates electricity from renewable energy sources have been increasing. Photocatalysts have the potential to solve the problems as photocatalysts reduce CO2 to methane, methanol and other products that can be used as fuels by using solar energy that is an abundant energy source in the world. For photocatalytic CO2 reduction, a variety of material structures and combinations are studied in addition to conventional material structures that are support, doping, and Z-scheme. Though several evaluation units that originate from diverse structures of composites and reactors have been studied, it is found that the evaluation methods need to be standardized. It is suggested that the light source for photocatalytic CO2 reduction should be artificial solar light. The unit used for the evaluation is proposed to be the conversion efficiency to demonstrate the ratio of the total energy of products (EP) to irradiation energy received at the reactor.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of wireless-power monitoring system for micro-inverter
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Nowadays Micro-Inverter (MI) has been popular to be implemented in various solar applications. For ensuring the MI works properly, monitoring of the real power condition is required. This paper presents a wireless-power monitoring system to measure the electrical parameters of the micro inverter such as RMS voltage, RMS current, instantaneous power, and power accumulation using MCP39F511. The measured data is transmitted by using ZigBee Pro with the multi-hop transmission capability. Moreover, a simple data format is also proposed for communicating between devices. All monitored data are stored in Network Operating Centre (NOC). As the result, the proposed system has been successfully implemented for MI in various rated power i.e. 100, 150, 200, and 250 Watt as a case study.

articleTitle: Energy management system employing harmony search algorithm for hybrid cogeneration
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Cogeneration is one of the microgrid implementation that is able to provide both electricity and heat energy simultaneously. Thus, it have been variously utilized in many energy generation plant including the commercial buildings like airport, hospital and hotel. However, a sophisticated control system is needed to ensure the objective of power flow in meeting the load requirement can be achieved. Energy management system which laid on the top of control hierarchy seems to have the ability to control and manage the energy flow in many type of microgrid especially cogeneration system. This presented article discuss a method of energy management system for the hybrid cogeneration system using the optimization approach. The objective of this proposed energy management system based optimization is to reduce the operational cost of hybrid cogeneration system that consist of PEMFC, photovoltaic and battery. Considering the parameters and variables such as weather conditions, load profile and fuel price, the optimization formulation is solved using the Harmony Search Algorithm which subjected to recognice constraints. Results of this study is leading to give the look up table which represent the generated power of each energy resources in 24 hours interval time. The simulation and analysis is performed in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of grid connected flyback inverter in the time discrete domain
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: A pre-design stage of power electronics circuits often involves simulation work to predict the real-world behaviour of a prototype. Simulating this behaviour would require a mathematical model to be derived. While extensive work has been done to mathematically describe the flyback inverter in the literature, the works are mainly for control analysis purposes. The study of mathematical derivations to allow for time-discrete circuit simulation behaviour remains scarce. This paper describes the mathematical model that enables the circuit simulation of the grid connected flyback inverter, in the time discrete domain. A grid connected flyback inverter prototype is constructed and the comparison between the experimental and the equation-based simulation is presented to provide verification to the mathematical model.

articleTitle: Cost benefit analysis for ZEB: Optimal capacity based on reliability, economy and diversification
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: A zero energy building (ZEB) has been envisioned to bring upon promising potential to address the issue of fuel crisis and environmental impacts from the use of fossil fuels. Presently, the off-grid ZEB has not gained significant international attention. However, the importance of the off-grid ZEB in providing local support during contingencies cannot be simply ignored. The main challenge of off-grid ZEB is in ensuring continuous electricity supply to end appliances on a basis of appropriate design of installation capacity size. As such, this paper firstly identifies the optimal capacity size for the renewable energy installation in the fictitious off-grid ZEB from the three perspectives including power reliability, economic importance and diversification of power configuration. And then, on a basis of identified optimal capacity size, the analysis of cost effectiveness of the off-grid ZEB is conducted by projecting the installation cost and electricity consumption in the building and by proposing the several scenarios for electricity tariff, and finally the return of investment of the proposed off-grid ZEB is evaluated.

articleTitle: Artificial neural network back-propagation based decision support system for ship fuel consumption prediction
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: In the maritime industry, there is the need of a decision support systems to take into account the combined effects of various factors involved in predicting ship fuel consumption to facilitate optimization of fuel consumption. In this paper, an artificial neural network back-propagation method with Levenberg-Marquardt is employed to construct the fuel efficiency profile of in-service tugboats operated along the Rejang River and the Straits of Malacca, Malaysia. The performance of the ANN is compared with multiple linear regression analysis (MLR) and exemplified with a case study. It can be concluded that ANN model produces better fit and accuracy than the MLR regression model in predicting complex and nonlinear relationship of the ship performance.

articleTitle: Maximum energy extraction for PV system using closed bracket technique
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: In this paper, Maximum Power Point (MPP) Tracking (MPPT) has been realized by a Combined Algorithm (CA). Here, a closed bracketed numerical method has been utilized for faster tracking and reducing the steady state error. The CA is an amalgamation of False Position Method (FPM), the close bracket numerical technique, and Hill Climbing method (HC). The two techniques in combination compliments each other as the HC determines the close bracket limits for FPM and the FPM compensates the steady state error of HC. In addition, this merger offers fast, simple, efficient and exact MPP tracking, compared to the conventional HC technique. To implement the HT a buck converter with a resistive load connected with a KC85T Solar Module has been employed. For software simulation, MATLAB Simulink software has been utilized. The simulation results display a commendable performance of the proposed CA.

articleTitle: Modeling of campus microgrid for off-grid application
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: The objectives of this study were to demonstrate the model of campus microgrid and illustrate the concept of peak shaving. SIMULINK SimPowerSystem tool is used to simulate the electrical circuit and control system of campus microgrid. The modeling of three major components, namely gas turbine generation, dynamic load and battery energy storage system were demonstrated in detail. The results have been revealed for Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS (UTP), an example university campus in Malaysia. This simulation model will be useful to carry the study on different ancillary services such as peak shaving, financial energy arbitrage, and investigating the effects of integrating renewable sources to microgrid.

articleTitle: Growth and characterization of Al-AlN films by plasma-assisted reactive evaporation
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Al-AlN thin films have been deposited on two different substrates of Si(111) and sapphire using Plasma Assisted-reactive evaporation method. The structural results revealed that the films grown on the both substrates were polycrystalline with better crystallinity for the films deposited on Si(111) substrate. Raman results showed that FWHM of disorder-activated B:(high) phonon mode is narrower for the film deposited on sapphire. A more compact morphology was observed from FESEM image of AlN/Si(111) compared to AlN/sapphire. FTIR spectra showed that the peak of A1(TO) mode shifted toward higher wavenumbers for AlN thin films grown on sapphire. The results could be effective in Si-based industry and devices such as adjusting solar absorption of a surface built up.

articleTitle: Techno-economic study of an innovative PV-hydrogen-biomass system for off-grid power supply
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems (HRES) can be considered as an alternative energy option to provide off-grid power generation. In this study, the development of an innovative HRES based on the integration of hydrogen generation from biomass gasification, renewable energy power generation, hydrogen generation from water electrolysis, and a fuel cell providing combined heat and power was proposed. The Techno-Economic study of the proposed system was carried out in order to support the annual electricity demand of a selected household in shinchi-machi in Fukushima prefecture. As indicated by results of the model in this study, the total annual electricity generation by the proposed HRES was estimated about 48 MWh with a total annual hydrogen generation of 2.7 ton. The Levelized Cost of Energy of the system, including both electricity and thermal energy, was estimated at about 0.49 $/kWh.

articleTitle: Recent advancement in heat pipe for stationary solar collectors
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: The increasing demand of energy can meet out through renewable source of energy. Hence it is necessary to focus on sustainable energy source. The solar energy is the prime source of energy, most available, eco-friendly and renewable to sustain the increasing energy demand. The solar energy is collected either through thermal based collectors or solar PV collectors. Moreover, heat pipe based solar collector is the most promising technology for various applications. Heat pipe is an advanced technology which has been proven to show higher thermal performance of solar collectors compared to conventional solar collectors. Due to high thermal performance, heat pipes becoming popular as passive energy transfer technology. This article lays out the comprehensive review of integration of heat pipe with stationary solar collectors. This manuscript comprised of mainly two parts: classification of heat pipes and heat pipes for stationary collectors. First part provides the information of types of heat pipes used for different applications and purpose followed by progress and development of heat pipes used in flat plate solar collector, evacuated tube solar collector and solar PV collector. Also, further studies are recommended for investigating the heat pipe in solar collectors by considering the economic issues. In addition to this major issues in heat pipe stationary collectors such as low heat removal factor (when less than ten heat pipes used in stationary collector), Increase complexity in design and small surface area of condenser are also discussed.

articleTitle: Investigation on quasi-Z-source inverter with hybrid energy storage for PMSM drive system
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: In electric vehicle (EV) drive system, having an energy sources with combination of high energy and power density characteristics is important. It enables the vehicle to travel at longer distance per charging cycle and demonstrates good response during acceleration and ability to recapture the energy during regenerative braking. This paper investigates on the newly proposed hybrid energy storage system on quasi-Z-source inverter (qZSI) for PMSM drive system. The objectives are to prove that bidirectional power flow in the drive system can be realized and the current stress on the battery can be reduced with the installation of the supercapacitor via the bidirectional DC-DC converter. Overall system configuration is presented together with the mathematical modelling analysis for the supercapacitor charging/discharging operation. Results from the simulation verification shows that the proposed method works satisfactorily according to the requirement.

articleTitle: Analysis of emitter layer diverse effects on electrical performance for prospective Si hybrid solar cell
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This paper presents two aspects of emitter layer engineering (ELE) in Si solar cells. Firstly Si emitter layer thickness and doping density influence on electrical performance followed by emitter materials choice for hetero-junction (HJ) solar cell (SC) design have been addressed. Due to dynamic loss at the interface, the crystalline silicon solar cell performance limits significantly. Emitter layer diverse parameters choices are key consideration to reduce the loss in Si hetero-junction hybrid solar cell (Si HHSC). Desired parameters of advance emitter materials thermo-electric conduction could link to band gap, Eg for improvement of Si HHSC performance. To realize the rudiments of advance emitter materials crucial parameters in HHSC; firstly self-emitter (due to similar thermo-electric property) has been considered for 100 μm Si wafer. Computer based Si solar cell with emitter layer diverse thickness and doping profile have been analyzed. It is realized that minimum emitter thickness and doping are healthier to electrical efficiency enhancements.

articleTitle: Forecasting of solar radiation in Malaysia using the artificial neural network and wavelet transform
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Production of solar energy by the photovoltaic panel is intermittent due to the fluctuation of solar radiation and this brings some problems to dispatcher or energy trader in dispatching, planning and scheduling the power network. This paper proposed the forecasting model of Artificial Neural Network (ANN), namely, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBFNN) with the combination of Wavelet Transform (WT) for the short-term forecasting of solar radiation. The performance of MLP and RBFNN was evaluated. The WT was then used to remove the noises and the accuracy of combining WT and ANN was determined. Results portrayed the outstanding performance of ANN as the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) values obtained were less than 5%. The performance comparison depicted that RBFNN was superior to the MLP and utilization of WT with MLP had revealed a good forecasting performance. Nonetheless, the RBFNN had not shown any significant accuracy changes when employing WT to filter the noises. This was due to the regularization properties of RBFNN to deal with the noisy data. Besides, the combination of 80%–20% of training and testing data had better performance than 70%–30% for forecasting purpose. In conclusion, the results are highly suggesting of employing ANN and WT to forecast the solar radiation.

articleTitle: Optimizing PEMFC model parameters using dragonfly algorithm: A performance study
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: The aims of optimizing the proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) model is to obtain the parameters used to plot the polarization curves. These curves are affected by many parameters related to the nonlinearities associated with the PEMFC electrochemical processes and the vital tools for simulation and evaluation of PEMFC. In this paper, Dragonfly Algorithm (DA) is proposed to identify these unknown parameters. The results related to two real systems, a single cell Ballard Mark V and the SR-12 PEMFC generator, illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. The DA presented competitive results when compared with the results of the other reported metaheuristics algorithms.

articleTitle: Electrical simulation of different photoactive layer thickness on organic heterojunction solar cell
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Organic bulk heterojunction solar cell based on poly 3-hexylthiophene (P3HT) and [6,6]-phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM) blend as photoactive layer had been electrically simulated and analyzed at different thickness using general-purpose photovoltaic device model (GPVDM) software. Conjugate polymer P3HT acted as an electron donor, whereby PCBM acts as an electron acceptor in the device. The electrical simulation is performed at three different thicknesses of 50 nm, 100 nm, and 200 nm with P3HT/PCBM blend and hetero-layer configurations, respectively. The simulation analysis clearly demonstrated that both device configurations exhibited current-voltage (I-V) characteristics with highest short-circuit current density (Jsc) value of 2.26 mA/cm2 with P3HT/PCBM of blend configuration at 200 nm thickness. However, an open-circuit voltage (Voc) and fill factor (FF) showed a constant value, which 0.55 V and 0.72 a.u., respectively, for both device configurations. The obtained value of solar cell parameters was then analysed and compared with experimental data. This simulation work strongly reveals that different thickness of photoactive material affects the electrical performance even in different organic solar cell configurations.

articleTitle: Control model development using TMS320F28335 microcontroller for high rated inverter and DC motor drive application
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This project describes a MATLAB control development in order to be tested in high power inverter and DC motor drive using TI microcontroller. The reason why two tests condition have been conducted is to test the application of inverter in to produce high power for the inverter output while the rectifier to test on the DC motor drive. This project is also to see the effectiveness of the TI controller board which is the TMS320F28335. The main features of this system is the ability of the controller which has been build in the TMS320F28335 for controlling the output current at the inverter and also to control the speed for DC motor application. Therefore, the Proportional Integral (PI) controller is used in those systems in order to ensure the current and speed outputs are same as the reference value that have been set in the Matlab/Simulink. At the end, all the results have shown a good agreement on the PI controller on the feedback response for both applications using TMS320F28335.

articleTitle: Binary nanocomposite of Co3O4 nanocubes supported on carbon matrix for supercapattery
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Herein, binary nanocomposite of reduced graphene intercalated with cobalt oxide nanocubes (rGO-Co3O4 nanocubes) was synthesized by hydrothermal process. The prepared nanocomposite is used for energy storage application. The crystallinity of the prepared nanocomposite was evaluated by X-ray diffraction while reduction of graphene oxide was confirmed by Raman spectroscopy. The surface morphology and particle size studies were done by field emission scanning electron microscopy. The asymmetric device was fabricated in configuration of rGO-Co3O4 nanocubes//activated carbon and its performance is evaluated by cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge discharge and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. The performance studies revealed that fabricated supercapattery was capable of delivering of 7.75 Wh.k−1 energy density at a power density of 996.42 W.kg−1. Additionally, supercapattery displayed excellent stability with capacity retention value above 90% after 3000 cycles.

articleTitle: Conducting polymers: New Arena in dye-sensitized solar cells
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSCs) have arose to be a cost-effective substitute for solar cells in energy storage application. This is due to its special features such as environmentally safe and stable, inexpensive manufacturing and simple fabrication technique. Although DSSC possessed high efficiency in power conversion, some of the material used leads toward its limitations. For instance, the use of platinum metal as counter electrode is highly cost and it tends towards corrosion. Moreover, the used of volatile liquid as electrolyte often result in leakage and low chemical stability. In order to overcome these drawbacks, conducting polymer (CPs) are employed as replacement material for counter electrode and liquid electrolyte since CPs is known with their numerous unique properties in various application. This overview highlighted the role of CPs especially polyaniline (PANI) and polypyrrole (PPy) in DSSCs that can improve its photovoltaic performance despite the challenges and future prospects in using CPs as substitute material.

articleTitle: Modelling of single power line by ATP-Draw for partial discharge signal measurement
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: PD is a main problem in insulation for high voltage (HV) that can lead to electrical degradation and damage to the insulation materials. PDs occur when the local electric field exceeds the threshold value and results in a partial breakdown of the surrounding medium. PD detection is formed in order to determine the condition of the insulating material in HV elements such as cables and covered conductor. Thus, this paper presents the modelling of power networks for PD signal measurement which involve a power source, transformer, power cables and loads. EMTP-ATP software is used in this study for modelling the single power line for PD measurement. Step by step to model the main component by ATP-Draw have been shown in this paper. The line communicates converter (LCC) based on J-Marti type is used to represent the power cables in this simulation. The advantages of using J-Marti model are; able to design a three-phase line cable in PD detection analysis and suitable for simulation of traveling wave phenomena in long transmission lines. The RC sensor model has been used in order to capture the PD signal on the single power line.

articleTitle: The direct power control for three-phase of AC-DC converter
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This paper presents the Direct Power Control (DPC) of grid connected three-phase AC-to-DC converter implemented in a regulated DC voltage power supply. Power electronic converters utilizing the diodes and thyristors as power switches are widely used in high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission system. However, the major drawback of using those power switches is the input currents are non-sinusoidal and consist of high harmonic current components. Therefore, the DPC is proposed in this work to improve the power quality of grid connected converter system. The main idea of this control method is direct control of active and reactive power. The measured current and voltage in the stationary reference frame (ajö-frame) are used to estimate the input instantaneous active and reactive power. The optimum switching state for the converter is determined from a switching look-up table. Steady state and dynamic performances of AC to DC converter are analysed before and after the implementation of the DPC method. It can be concluded that after using the DPC method, the three-phase input currents are almost sinusoidal thus, the current total harmonic distortion can be reduced. The converter operation is maintained at unity power factor by supplying zero reference reactive power.

articleTitle: Remote desktop power management system using single-board computer
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: In this paper, remote desktop power management system is proposed for remote power management of multiple desktop computers. This system will enable desktop computer to be restarted, switch on or off in the event of computer freeze or based on user input by controlling the power to the desktop computer. The system has the ability to monitor the environment parameters such as the temperature, humidity, and air quality surrounding the desktop computer. This remote desktop power management system can be accessed primarily using website interface. This system will save time and cost as less on-site maintenance and monitoring is needed.

articleTitle: Calibration of a commercial building energy simulation models using energy and weather data
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This research emphasizes on energy and weather data of Innoplex building as a case study where the cooling system is the main system to maintain comfort condition throughout the building areas entirely. The objective of this research is to reduce the accuracy of the input parameter changes by determining the highest contributing factors towards energy segments and proposing the energy calibration measures. The calibration was carried out on the EnergyPlus simulation tool which integrated with Sefaira Architecture web-performance. To evaluate the accuracy of the model used, Mean Bias Error and Coefficient of Variation of the Root Mean Squared Error were calculated. The results obtained earlier must be consistent with ASHRAE guideline 14 limits for a model to be considered calibrated. Energy calibration of a commercial building is affected by a few factors that can be identified through different amount of monthly energy consumption between simulated and measured data based on the electricity bills produced at the end of a specific period of time. In this study, the calibration results from the simulation are evaluated and the lowest index will be selected as the best strategy to improve energy performance.

articleTitle: PLL-less SRF technique for operation of SAPF under unbalanced and distorted supply voltage
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Shunt active power filter (SAPF) has been recognized as a feasible solution to current harmonics issues. In its controller, due to structure simplicity, synchronous reference frame (SRF) technique is best suited to be applied in generating reference current. However, the existing SRF algorithm performs inefficiently due to limitations of numerical low-pass filter (LPF). Besides, the existing algorithm is as yet considered to have excessive features which are not required in the procedure of generating reference current. Most importantly, its dependency on traditional phase-locked loop (PLL) has greatly degraded its effectiveness when the source voltage is unbalanced and/or distorted. Therefore, this paper presents a PLL-less SRF algorithm for generating reference current to effectively control performance of a SAPF developed based on three-level neutral-point-clamped (NPC) inverter. Specifically, three notable refinements are implemented: (1) eliminate the traditional use of LPF by replacing it with a mathematical-based average current detector; (2) reduce algorithm complexity by removing excessive features; (3) eliminate synchronization error of PLL by integrating a new self-tuning-filter (STF)-based synchronization technique. The proposed algorithm is created and assessed in MATLAB-Simulink. Simulation and experimental results are provided, demonstrating superiority of the proposed PLL-less SRF algorithm over the existing SRF algorithm.

articleTitle: Superior self-cleaning glass through hydrophobic and superhydrophilic coating for outdoor applications
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: The wettability of the coating surface is strongly exhibit as practical approach for self-cleaning purposes. In this paper, a transparent hydrophobic nano-CaCO3/ modified PDMS coating with hydrophobic properties and superhydrophilic nano-TiO2 coating with good self-cleaning properties have been successfully developed for glass substrate application. The coating was applied onto glass plates using sponges and tested against water contact angle (WCA) measurement. The hydrophobic coating achieves the WCA as high as 117±2° and superhydrophilic coating achieves water contact angle as low as 4.9±0.5°. For superhydrophilic surface, the applied dirt liquids tend to spread across the coating surface. For hydrophobic coating, the applied dirt liquids are completely removed from the coating surface. The prepared-coating also exhibits an excellent anti-fogging and anti-water streak behavior due to the absence of water-streaks and water-droplets are appeared on both coated glass surfaces after impacting to water-spraying and fog testing. In conclusion, this hydrophobic coating and superhydrophilic coating will be highly practical for outdoor applications of photovoltaic panel.

articleTitle: Syntheses of azomethine-thiophene monomers for potential application in energy storage devices
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Newly design thiophene monomers containing azomethine base moieties for the preparation of side chain liquid crystalline polymers were successfully synthesized. The proposed monomers are conducting in nature, making it as potential material for energy storage devices. The compounds were characterized by Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR), 1H nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and thermal gravimetric analysis (TGA). The presence of azomethine groups found at 1617 cm−1 in FTIR, NMR confirms singlet peaks at δ∼9.5 ppm and TGA data shows thermal cleavage occurred at 166.6–269.93°C. The n-type properties combined with the inherently weak emission and high thermal stability thus make the polythiophenoazomethine suitable candidates for hole and electron transporting materials.

articleTitle: Integrated renewable energy micro-grid for meeting peak hours demand
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: In the TNB-based conventional system, the power demand varies randomly depending upon seasons and months of the year including festive occasions, reaching peak in some hours of days of some months. Sometime a heavy demand (in MW) falls at a time of a day. Such heavy energy demands need to be transported from far-away power stations over long lengthy transmissions causing energy loss not less than 20% in most of the cases. This paper presents load demand variation scenario, identifying peaks, and finally suggesting a strategy for meeting the peak demand from Renewable Energy Sources (RES) of solar and wind. An integrated RES-based microgrid is suggested with analytical and simulation results showing how the peak demand is being met from alternative sources of solar. The results of this paper find applications in suggesting RES-based generations for distributed locations within the low-voltage distribution network of Malaysian Electric Utility Tenaga Nasional Berhad.

articleTitle: Influence of concentration of polyaniline (PANI) as counter electrode in dye sensitized solar cell
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Platinum (Pt) as a precious metal has high photoelectric response as it is highly conducting and electroactive material used as a counter electrode in dye sensitized solar cell (DSSC). Herein, polyaniline (PANI) is synthesized by simple oxidative polymerization approach and is used as a counter electrode in DSSC. The performance of PANI coated on FTO counter electrode is evaluated by varying the thickness of film prepared by spin coating and doctor blade techniques. It is found that PANI-3 (20 mg concentration) counter electrode demonstrated enhanced redox activity using redox couple Ferricyanide analyte in 0.1 M KCl as an electrolyte as compared to its counter electrodes. The structural, morphological and optical properties of PANI were confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD), field emission scanning electron microscope (FESEM), high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM), UV-vis spectrophotometer and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR). The photovoltaic performance of fabricated electrodes for DSSCs was examined by linear swap voltammetry LSV and cyclic voltammetry (CV). It was found that unaided PANI-3 counter electrode showed good electro catalytic activity which was approaching to the catalytic activity of commercially available Pt. By doping PANI with some other metal and metal oxide materials the catalytic activity and efficiency can be enhanced.

articleTitle: Fuel quality index of transesterified and nontransestried oil samples of Mustard and Ricebran oil
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This research aimed to investigate the potential assessment of normally used cooking oil (Mustard oil (MO) and Rice bran oil (RBO) as a biodiesel after transesterification process and find the optimum conditions for this process. Unused oil (0th sample/control) and used oil (after10th cycle of heating and cooling) were used as experimental sample in this study. Two temperature ranges were used i.e. 27±2°C and 150±5°C for cooling and heating of oil samples respectively. Fuel quality indexes (FQI) were analyzed in reference of biodiesel for used and unused cooking oil samples (control). Similarly, control and samples after 10th cycle with selected cooking oils samples (1st and 10th only) after transesterification process were also evaluated for fuel quality.
