On comparison, before and after transestrification with 10th cycle of heating and cooling oil samples of MO and RBO, shows a remarkable change in the value of density, viscosity and little change with iodine number and flash point in comparison to control and 1st cycle of heating and cooling of oil samples. Result showed a similar trend in value like commercial biodiesel after evaluating FQI. On comparative basis, RBO (10th cycle sample after transestrification) was found to be more feasible as diesel fuel.

articleTitle: Design investigation of high reliable HE-FSM for electromechanical actuator used in aircrafts
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: In this paper, the requirements and challenges of designing a hybrid excitation (HE) dual stator motor, which can be used in electromechanical directly driven actuator for aircraft applications are presented. The use of directly driven actuator system offers the advantage of eliminating the transitional gearbox from the system. Besides, it also holds advantages in terms of lower components count and is able to reduce the jamming probability. Moreover, an electrically supplied actuator gives the distinct benefits to escaping the both hydraulic and combustion supply systems with all their related detriments. The overall key purposes of the designing an electrically supplied actuator are a high level of actuator integration in order to decrease the weight and the volume, fault tolerance capability, and high torque density production. For these explanations, a new sort of electrical motor has been familiarized since last decade, which is known as flux switching machine (FSM). FSMs carry all its active excitation sources on the stator side leaving the rotor as a robust peace of iron structure. Using DE sources of PM and field excitation (FE) machine produces more torque density and known as hybrid excitation (HEFSM). Since HE machines provide high torque-to-weight ratios and high efficiency during research in the last decade. However, due to series HE machines the FE flux lines passes through the permanent magnets (PMs). Therefore, as a result of the low permeability of the PMs, the magnetic reluctance of the magnetic path for the excitation coil is quite high which cause the degrading of flux regulation effect. Hence, in this paper a arrangement of segmented rotor dual stator (DS) HEFSM using parallel HE is proposed as well as analysed. The suggested structure of DS HEFSM in this paper shows the simple structure which consists only three active sources of FECs and three PMs. 2D finite element analysis (FEA) method has been applied to analysis the proposed structure. Coil test analysis at open circuit condition, is investigated to validate the operating principle of the proposed HEFSM model. Furthermore, at short circuit condition, the load analysis is examined to ascertain the overall outcome in terms of torque and power.

articleTitle: Latent heat retrieval techniques in PV/T collectors
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This paper critically reviews the retrieving of latent heat techniques particularly categorized as static and dynamic mode during charging/discharging cycle for lowering the operating temperature of the PV modules through an integrated device commonly known as PV/T collectors. Various PV/T collectors (air/water/nano-fluid) have been designed and developed globally depending upon the type of working medium and the utility. This paper basically reviews the techniques concerned with the use of latent heat in PV/T systems. On one hand the static mode comprises the use of latent heat of fusion through phase change materials (PCMs), while dynamic mode constitutes the use of heat pipes/loop heat pipes where condensed vapors of low boiling temperature fluid was used to retrieve their respective latent heats. The paper also identifies the significant role of latent heat in thermal engineering for various applications.

articleTitle: SNO2 and TIO2 coatings toward decreasing the surface temperature of solar cells
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Transparent SnO2 and TiO2 coatings are developed in a binder network consisting of 3-aminopropyl triethoxysilane (H2N-(CH2)3-Si-(OC2H5)3) and methyltrimethoxy silane (Si-CH3-(OCH3)3) with ratio 1:1. The formulation method was cost-effective, produces good transparency, clear and managed to dry at room temperature. The coating mixtures were applied onto the acrylic sheets by using sponges and they were sent for structural and thermal characterizations. The Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM) topography showed that the both particles are well-dispersed and in good agreement with the binder system. Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDX) study confirmed that both metal oxide particles managed to blend well into the mesoporous network of the coating solution in separate events. In a thermal study by using thermocouples, TiO2 coating gave an excellent result for thermal-decreasing ability with a decrease in surface temperature of solar cell by 10°C from the uncoated solar cell after approximately one hour. However, the thermal characterization showed a negative result against the solar cell with SnO2 coating as there is a rise in the surface temperature of solar cell which is more than the one with uncoated sheet. Overall, TiO2 coating showed positive results for both structural and thermal characterizations while SnO2 coating possesses good structural properties but poor thermal-decreasing ability for solar cells.

articleTitle: Evaluation of five compensation circuits for electric vehicle inductively coupled power transfer (ICPT)
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: This paper analyzed and evaluated the output power and efficiency characteristics from five new compensation circuits for inductively coupled power transfer (ICPT) system. These compensations are series-series (SS), double-sided inductor capacitor capacitor (LCC), inductor capacitor capacitor-series (LCC-S), SS detuned and inductor capacitor-series (LC-S). The parameter tuning of all passive components for compensation circuits was presented in equations form before circuit analysis. All topologies were analyzed with inductive power transfer (IPT) equivalent circuit model using Kirchhoff Law theorem and matrix operation in MATLAB platform. Based on simulation result, although the SS compensation scheme generated the highest output power at low coupling coefficient, followed by an LC-S scheme, the flexibility of LC-S tuning has the advantage over than the SS scheme. Other topologies were underperformed in output power yet each of them has its specialty according to their purposed design.

articleTitle: Investigation on effect of MWCNT on microstructural and thermal properties of paraffin based PCM
publicationTitle: 5th IET International Conference on Clean Energy and Technology (CEAT2018)
abstract: Latent heat is the most important property for phase change material (PCM) as thermal energy storage material. It is closely related to the internal properties of the material. The aim of this article is to examine the effect of multi walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) on the microstructural and thermal properties of a paraffin based PCM and their influence on energy storage. Thermal stability, functional group and morphology of a pure PCM and MWCNT mixed PCM have been analysed using DSC, FTIR, and FESEM, respectively. Microstructural observation shows that MWCNT is homogeneously incorporated into the PCM matrix. FTIR spectra of pure and MWCNT mixed PCM are similar, indicating that there was no chemical interaction. It was found from DSC result that MWCNT/RT44HC composite PCM shows a 2.7% increase in latent heat of fusion. The newly introduced composite material is suitable for energy storage in solar thermal and solar photovoltaic thermal applications.
